name: find
summary: Searches for files in a directory tree.
description: Walks the given directories recursively and applies tests (name, type, size, date…) to each file. Files that pass every test are printed, or have an action applied to them (-delete, -exec). A quirk: its options are written with a single dash but are whole words (-name, -type).

options.description: File name matching the pattern (wildcards * ? [ ] allowed, put it in quotes).
File type: f (file), d (directory), l (symbolic link).
Size: +10M (more than 10 MiB), -1k (less than 1 KiB), 100c (exactly 100 bytes).
Modified N days ago: -7 (less than 7 days), +30 (more than 30 days).
Exact permissions (644) or at least these permissions (-u+x).
Goes down at most N levels below the starting paths.
Applies the tests only from N levels deep.
Modified more recently than the given file.
Runs a command on each result; {} is replaced by the file, and the command ends with \; (one call per file) or + (one grouped call).
Deletes the files found. Use it last, after checking the results without this option.
Logical OR between two tests (by default, tests are combined with AND).

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: Starting directory (or directories). Default: the current directory.

examples.explanation: Every .log file under the current directory.
Deletes the files in /tmp not modified for more than 7 days.

dangerNote: With -delete or -exec rm, a pattern mistake can delete many files. Run the command without the action first to check the list.
